Creator approval was explicitly given and the real local Compiler birth completed successfully at 2026-09-03T00:58:44.622215Z against pinned Hermes commit 30b83ab7b1f194503de9f5545d88c81c4db91e3f. The first full Heartbeat sealed the two-part Primer, initialized the VCW and Layer 0 baseline, and left the MIND unconfigured without making a provider call. Post-birth verification passed (4 physical layers, 5 records). Private identity, key, Primer, VCW contents, and organism state remain local and Git-ignored. The Windows identity key ACL was hardened during the gate; the reusable fix landed through #11.

Completed by #22. The audit found that terminal and gateway turns already traverse the common turn seams and failures are already represented by completed-turn status. Added only the two missing true session-shutdown nerves, corrected the former per-turn session label, rebuilt the public seed, and passed all protected checks.

Released as v2.0.0-alpha.2 after PRs #13, #22, and #23 passed the full protected matrix. The release workflow independently rebuilt and verified the pinned Hermes construction, Python distributions, public delta bundle, test report, SBOM, and checksums. This remains a construction prerelease and does not claim native Hermes runtime certification or birth.

Progress merged in #25: the resident watch now recovers interrupted host Heartbeats, performs a full startup Heartbeat, wakes with a full unscheduled Heartbeat on a committed COMMUNICATION.TXT save, and performs scheduled full Heartbeats on an independent cadence. Framework tests pass on Windows and Linux across Python 3.11-3.13. Remaining before closure: actual disposable user-level registration/startup/removal certification on Windows and Linux. No resident registration was installed on the creator machine.

Progress merged in #30: the resident launcher now loads the NEST-local organs using isolated Python, with no fallback to the globally installed constructor. Missing or redirected organ directories stop before registration.

All 73 tests pass on Windows and Linux across Python 3.11–3.13. The new real subprocess test uses authenticated encryption and proves startup, committed communication with no configured MIND, forced process stop and restart, recovery of a pending host receipt, no duplicate conversation response after restart, unchanged sealed Primer, and native Body execution after stopping Heart. CodeQL and pinned Hermes delta/native parity also pass.

Remaining: actual Task Scheduler/systemd registration, automatic crash restart, graceful shutdown, and removal. OS registration is still mocked in unit tests; the process test does not install a resident service. Python and cryptography remain prerequisites. PLAN.md records this boundary. Issue remains open pending native service evidence.

Updated-manual reconciliation is in PR #31 and `docs/MANUAL_21_RECONCILIATION.md`.
PR #30's real NEST-local process/restart/communication evidence is preserved.

The manual sharpens this issue's remaining gates: bounded graceful shutdown,
explicit restart policy, storage-enforced stale-writer refusal, and one serialized
Body mutation port. Existing file locks and a forced process restart are useful
but do not prove those stronger guarantees. Native Task Scheduler/systemd
certification remains open; no creator-machine registration is authorized here.

Updated-manual reconciliation is in PR #31 and `docs/MANUAL_21_RECONCILIATION.md`.
Existing mapper/innervation tests and the pinned Hermes seed remain preserved.

The additional acceptance detail is explicit: static anatomy stays distinct from
authorized, windowed runtime circulation evidence. Include cross-process/scheduled
loops, critical low-volume validation/commit boundaries, supported causal links,
configuration fingerprints and unknown regions. Verified bindings need bounded
nonblocking ingress/loss reporting, grants rechecked at consumption, drift
suspension and action-origin feedback control. No traditional plugin model is
introduced, and source inventory is not claimed as complete live coverage.

PR #32 advances this issue without closing it. The CLI now supports cooperative
signal-managed stop between full Heartbeats, restores previous handlers, and
keeps failed in-flight work visibly failed. Maintenance is considered despite
communication-file observation failure; simultaneous due/message wakes use one
full scheduled beat.

Evidence: controlled-clock/callback tests across Windows/Linux, plus actual Linux
SIGTERM delivery to a disposable NEST-local runtime. Existing real encrypted
process/restart and native Body/Primer checks remain. `docs/RESIDENT_HEART.md`
records precise coverage and remaining gaps.

Still open: native Task Scheduler/systemd lifecycle and registration ownership,
fenced single-writer storage, atomic publication/recovery, asynchronous
cancellation and a hard overall shutdown deadline. Windows force termination
does not count as graceful shutdown. No creator-machine resident installation.

Progress: PR #33 passed all required checks and adds registration-boundary safeguards, with PLAN.md, the coding contract, lifecycle evidence and the reproducible Hermes seed synchronized.

- Collision refusal; no forced replacement of Windows tasks or Linux unit files.
- Pending intent preserved before OS mutation; failures retain evidence rather than attempting blind rollback.
- Removal validates NEST-derived receipt targets, unchanged runner, current task owner/action/privilege or exact loaded unit and no overrides. Linux verification precedes service start; Windows stop failure prevents deletion.
- Status distinguishes receipt evidence from running-state proof and retains visibility when the runner is missing.
- Local Windows verification: 188 passed, 2 platform skips; Ruff, public-tree audit and seed hashes passed. GitHub Windows/Linux Python 3.11–3.13, CodeQL and pinned-Hermes gates passed.

Issue remains open. Next is real native Task Scheduler/systemd install/start/stop/removal evidence in disposable environments, including actual XML, already-stopped behavior and partial-removal recovery. Automatic restart, transactional recovery, stale-writer fencing and bounded in-flight cancellation are not certified by these fixture tests. No service was installed on the creator's PC and no real SELF was changed.

Progress in PR #34: real native lifecycle tests now replace a previously fixture-only evidence gap.

Final source head `ff9a24d` passed both native jobs in [run 34157765506](https://github.com/jodydugas-ctrl/MantleOS2/actions/runs/34157765506), on disposable Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows Server 2025 runners with Python 3.12. Failed initial starts retain pending evidence; failed verification prevents starting the task.

body:
Integration cleanup pass found and fixed two release-publication loose ends before merge:

- the final v1.0 workflow had duplicate job-level `permissions` mappings, which made the workflow definition invalid on the integration head;
- release publication authority was previously held by the whole final-certification job. It is now isolated into a separate `publish-release` job that runs only on a successful push to `main`, with `contents: write` scoped only to that job.

The certification job now has only `contents: read`, `actions: read`, and `checks: read`; its source-head lineage query receives the GitHub token only on that main-only step. The publication job re-downloads the sealed release artifact, verifies `SHA256SUMS.txt`, verifies the aggregate certificate is PASS and bound to the exact main commit, then creates the immutable `v1.0.0` release.

Current integration head: `9960295d4c014c056b2fe4ad37a53c47ffcaa1a8`.

I am holding the merge until the exact current head has successful broader-calibration and independent-reconstruction stage evidence; this preserves the release workflow's exact-head lineage guarantee rather than inheriting checks from an earlier candidate.
